I will start from what I did in past years and only adjust a little. On 6 mu, I cannot gamble too much. Fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too hard and the crop stays small, that loss is worse. Here in Quzhou with well water, I do not fear drought as much, so I will push the cabbage and Chinese cabbage a bit more, because those crops pay back when they grow fast and head well. Chili and kidney bean I will keep on smaller area, because they need more watching and picking. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I already saw good stands and better uniformity on other people’s fields, but I will not go too fancy. For cabbage and Chinese cabbage, I will put more base fertilizer and then topdress after they start taking off. For kidney bean, I will hold nitrogen lower, otherwise it runs too much vine. I will plough before the first crop, then mostly use rotary tillage between crops to save labor. With two people in the house, I have to keep the plan workable, not too scattered.
